argument_markdown:
Source-backed inputs.

ATT-0066, dual-confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies: the h0(L)∈{3,4} stratification (CLM-0066-2 and CLM-0066-3); the projective-bundle identification I_k≅P((π_*L|_{B_k})^∨) on each reduced constant-h0 stratum (CLM-0066-4); the global Abel–Jacobi/Hilbert model across the jump (CLM-0066-5); and the stack-level finite étale S_6-torsor tilde-I→I^dist (CLM-0066-6). The reducedness caveat emphasized by REV-0116 is retained, and no negative disclaimer in ATT-0066 is promoted to an existence theorem.

Proved step 1: projective-bundle components.

Fix k and an irreducible component Y of B_k. Over a nonempty trivializing open U⊂Y, the inverse image is U×P^{k−1}, hence irreducible. Because the projective-bundle projection is open and surjective, the inverse image of the dense open U is dense in the full inverse image over Y. Thus P((π_*L|_Y)^∨) is irreducible. The inverse images of the irreducible components of B_k are closed, cover I_k, and none contains another because their images in B_k do not; they are therefore precisely the irreducible components of I_k. On a trivializing open, the standard Krull-dimension formula gives dim P((π_*L|_Y)^∨)=dim(Y)+k−1.

Proved step 2: monodromy controls the ordered components.

Put G=S_6 and restrict the ATT-0066 torsor to V. Choose a geometric point v̄ of V and one point of the fibre. The right G-torsor structure identifies that fibre with G. Étale monodromy commutes with the right G-action, so after this choice it acts on G by left multiplication through a homomorphism ρ_V:π_1^ét(V,v̄)→G, well-defined up to conjugacy. Connected components of a finite étale cover correspond to monodromy orbits. If H_V=im(ρ_V), its orbits on G have size |H_V| and number [G:H_V]. Since V is normal and connected, it is irreducible; finite étale covers preserve normality, so every connected component of the restricted torsor is normal and connected and hence irreducible. Each such component is finite étale of degree |H_V| over V and has dimension dim(V). The two extreme cases follow immediately: [G:H_V]=720 iff H_V={1}, and [G:H_V]=1 iff H_V=G.

Computational hypotheses.

None. No finite experiment or point count is used to prove the theorem.

Gaps and exact-target status.

The theorem supplies an exact test, not the missing input: the irreducible components of B_3 and B_4 and the images H_V are not computed. Existence or density of the distinct-support locus on each relevant component is also not proved. Therefore no component decomposition of the full image in M_{6,6}, no associated local-system decomposition, and no statement about W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is obtained.

claims.justification: ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, gives the projective-bundle model on reduced strata. Irreducibility and the component bijection follow from local triviality over dense opens; the dimension formula is the standard projective-bundle formula.
claims.statement: For k∈{3,4}, irreducible components of the reduced stratum B_k correspond bijectively to irreducible components of I_k, and a component over Y has dimension dim(Y)+k−1.

claims.justification: ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies the finite étale S_6-torsor. The Galois-category classification identifies connected components with π_1^ét-orbits; normality turns connected components into irreducible components.
claims.statement: For connected normal V⊂I^dist, the irreducible components of the ordered incidence above V are the monodromy orbits on S_6 and number [S_6:H_V].

claims.justification: This is the specialization of CLM-0082-2 to H_V={1} and H_V=S_6. It shows that neither proposed extreme follows from the deck group alone.
claims.statement: The ordered incidence over V has 720 irreducible components iff its S_6-monodromy is trivial, and is irreducible iff its monodromy image is all of S_6.

claims.justification: ATT-0066 explicitly leaves component analysis open, while REV-0110 and REV-0116 do not add a component or monodromy computation.
claims.statement: The actual irreducible-component sets of B_3 and B_4 and the actual subgroups H_V are not determined by the verified dependency package.

claims.justification: The working-context constraints forbid inferring Tate type from rational S_6-representation theory, and this attempt supplies no such cohomological calculation.
claims.statement: No Tate or non-Tate conclusion for the exact RED-0001 group follows from the component test without geometric monodromy and cohomology-with-local-coefficients calculations.

gap_markers.statement: The irreducible components of the balanced h0 strata B_3 and B_4 are not computed. Classical Hurwitz irreducibility cannot be substituted for this calculation.
For each relevant connected normal V⊂I^dist, the subgroup H_V⊂S_6 is not computed; hence the formula [S_6:H_V] is not specialized to a numerical component count.
Nonemptiness and density of the distinct-support incidence on every relevant geometric fibre or base component remain unproved.
No cohomology with the monodromy local systems is computed, so the exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is not shown to be Tate and no surviving non-Tate summand is exhibited.

novelty_claims: Provides an independently proved necessary-and-sufficient monodromy test for the proposed ordered component decompositions: the component number is [S_6:H], rather than automatically 720 or automatically one.

Separates the two component problems exactly: projective-bundle geometry transfers irreducible components from each reduced h0 stratum, while ordering introduces only the additional finite étale monodromy-orbit calculation.

proof_dependencies.role: Verified C66-GEO-H0 dependency supplying CLM-0066-2 through CLM-0066-6: the h0 strata, reduced-stratum projective bundles, global Abel–Jacobi incidence, and stack-level ordered finite étale S_6-torsor.
First independent confirmation of ATT-0066 and all CLM-0066-1 through CLM-0066-6, with the weak normalization retained as a hypothesis.
Second independent confirmation of ATT-0066; its reduced-base Grauert caveat and disclaimer warning are enforced in the theorem scope.

summary: The balanced Abel–Jacobi incidence has exactly the same irreducible-component decomposition as its reduced constant-h0 base strata, with the expected projective-bundle dimension shifts. Over a connected normal piece of the distinct-support incidence, the ordered incidence has [S6:H] irreducible components, where H is the actual geometric monodromy image in S6. Thus the proposed extremes of 720 components and one component are respectively equivalent to trivial and full S6 monodromy; neither follows merely from the existence of the S6-torsor. The actual monodromy and base-stratum component sets remain open, and no conclusion about RED-0001 is asserted.

theorem_scope.base: locally Noetherian over a characteristic-zero field; B_3 and B_4 are required to be reduced and finite-dimensional; the monodromy clause is applied only over a connected normal locally Noetherian substack V
theorem_scope.exclusions: No irreducibility of B_3 or B_4 is asserted; no monodromy image is computed; no nonemptiness or density of I^dist on every fibre is asserted; no component, stabilizer, closure, monomorphism, dimension, or codimension statement is made for the image in M_{6,6}; and no Hodge, weight, purity, local-system, or Tate conclusion is drawn.
theorem_scope.generality: fibrewise balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl families within the precise ATT-0066 scope, including its weak relative-canonical normalization hypothesis

theorem_statement: Component-and-monodromy test for the balanced tetragonal incidence. Assume the fibrewise balanced genus-6 degree-4 Casnati–Ekedahl hypotheses and the weak relative-canonical normalization carried by ATT-0066. Let B_3 and B_4 be the h0(L)=3 and h0(L)=4 strata, let I be the global degree-six Abel–Jacobi incidence, and assume each B_k is reduced, locally Noetherian, and finite-dimensional. For k in {3,4}, the projection I_k:=I×_B B_k→B_k induces a bijection between irreducible components: an irreducible component Y⊂B_k corresponds to P((π_*L|_Y)^∨), which has dimension dim(Y)+k−1. Now let V be any connected normal locally Noetherian substack of I^dist, and let H_V⊂S_6 be the image, defined up to conjugacy, of the étale monodromy representation on a geometric fibre of the finite étale S_6-torsor tilde-I_V→V. Then tilde-I_V has exactly [S_6:H_V] irreducible components; every component maps finite étale of degree |H_V| to V and has dimension dim(V). Consequently tilde-I_V has 720 irreducible components exactly when H_V is trivial, and it is irreducible exactly when H_V=S_6.
